# Privacy Policy Template

Six files, ~25 KB. **One document in two hand-maintained renderings**: `PRIVACY_POLICY.md` (the
canonical text, 15 sections, 186 lines) and `index.html` (a self-contained responsive page, 214
lines, inline `<style>`, light/dark via `prefers-color-scheme`, **zero external requests**). No
build step, no generator, no framework, no JavaScript. See [[self-contained-single-file-html]].

**Status: active and shipped.** "A template, and Pages is live" (interview, 2026-07-28). It is a
reusable policy template published at the project's GitHub Pages URL —
[[one-reusable-policy-not-per-project]] and [[host-on-github-pages]].

**Evidence gap, recorded honestly:** the repo contains **no `CNAME`, no Pages workflow and no
deployment artefact of any kind**. The README's "(done)" refers to the push, not to Pages being
enabled. The live-URL claim rests on the interview alone; `confidence: high` on the claim because
the user confirmed it, with nothing in the tree corroborating it.

## What it covers — and what it does not

**Chronology rules out both products.** `privacy-policy` was created 2026-02-28 and its full policy
text landed 2026-07-10. [[farely]]'s first commit is 2026-07-12; [[stickfps]]'s is 2026-07-24. The
policy predates them by roughly 4.5 and 5 months, so **it covers neither**.

The content confirms it independently. The policy's subject is a *website*: it discloses only
GitHub Pages server logs plus inbound email, states "None set by this Service by default" for
cookies, and names no other third-party processor. Farely is an Android app with an accessibility
service, on-device inference, an optional cloud-vision path and a third-party events feed — and it
carries its **own** privacy documentation, which never links here. Stickfps has accounts and a
database; the policy discloses neither. Two independent lines of evidence agree, so this is
`confidence: high`.

## The legal content, as concepts

[[data-minimisation]] — named and applied in §4, and the load-bearing principle of the whole
document · [[gdpr-legal-bases]] — Art. 6 bases mapped per processing purpose in §5 ·
[[controller-vs-processor]] — defined in §3 and applied to the host in §7.

Also present, not given their own pages: the CCPA/CPRA no-sale/no-share attestation with a
12-month lookback (§8), data-subject rights with response windows of 30 days GDPR / 45 days CCPA
(§9), the Polish supervisory authority named by name (UODO), international transfers via Standard
Contractual Clauses (§10), retention limits (§11), a children's-privacy floor of 13 — or 16 in
parts of the EU (§13), an LGPD/PIPEDA catch-all (§9.3), and an annual-review commitment (§14).

## Findings

- **The only genuinely long-running history in the group.** 8 commits over 2026-02-28 → 2026-07-25,
  in three phases with a **~4.5-month dead gap**: three commits in three minutes in February whose
  wording and rename-in-place pattern are characteristic of GitHub web-UI edits (a placeholder repo
  created in the browser); four commits in about one second on 2026-07-10 replacing the placeholder
  with the real policy, the HTML rendering, the licence and the expanded README; and one lone
  screenshot commit on 2026-07-25.
- **The 2026-07-10 burst is 24 minutes before the identical licence/badge pair in
  [[physics-exam-prep]] and [[computer-project-management]]** — one consolidation session across
  three repos, not a product launch. Per the interview these dates are "just cleaning up local
  folders"; see [[import-finished-work-into-git]].
- **Two renderings, maintained by hand, with nothing preventing drift.** No generator turns the
  markdown into the HTML. They agree structurally today; nothing enforces that they will.
  Compare [[documentation-drift]], which is what happens when this arrangement is left alone.
- **The README is a product tour, not a code README** — badges, a light/dark preview table, "What's
  inside", publishing steps, a reuse checklist, licence, disclaimer. [[readme-as-guided-tour]].
- **The disclaimer is inline, not a footnote.** "It is **not legal advice**" appears in both the
  README and the closing line of the policy itself — [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].

## Security note

The owner's email address appears four times in `PRIVACY_POLICY.md` (§1, §9, §15), once in
`index.html` §15 and once in the README footer. **It is deliberately not reproduced anywhere in
this wiki.** The repo is public, so this is a disclosure the owner chose; that does not make it
this wiki's to copy.
